metadata.title: Secure‑SDLC IoMT / Clinical Safety SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan specializing Secure‑SDLC for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) and clinical software development where patient safety, clinical authority, and regulatory compliance supersede delivery speed and automation.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP inherits Secure‑SDLC Platform rules and applies additional clinical safety and regulatory constraints.

system-characteristics.system-description: This environment governs development of medical device firmware, clinical software, therapy‑control logic, diagnostic systems, and monitoring platforms that may directly or indirectly affect patient outcomes. It enforces patient‑safety supremacy, strict recall handling, and clinical authorization boundaries.

props.name: domain
props.remarks: Applies to network-connected medical and clinical software.

props.name: regulatory-anchor
props.remarks: Medical software development is governed by regulatory and quality standards outside SDLC authority.

props.name: state-assumption
props.remarks: Clinical actions may produce irreversible patient harm.

props.name: delivery-frequency
props.remarks: Changes are infrequent and heavily validated.

props.name: automation-level
props.remarks: CI/CD automation is limited for clinical software.

props.name: implicit-deploy
props.remarks: No SDLC outcome may automatically deploy or activate clinical software.

props.name: implicit-therapy
props.remarks: Signed, tested, or assured software must not enable therapy or actuation.

props.name: authority-source
props.remarks: Only clinical and regulatory authority can enable medical software.

props.name: recall-precedence
props.remarks: Device or software recall overrides all SDLC outcomes.

system-implementation.remarks: IoMT SDLC is implemented through Secure‑SDLC patterns with patient‑safety dominance. SDLC outputs remain advisory and are gated by clinical approval, regulatory clearance, and Secure‑Resilience eligibility before any use.

components.title: SDLC Core
components.remarks: Defines SDLC artifact legitimacy without granting clinical authority.

components.title: SDLC Identity and Attribution
components.remarks: Maintains accountability without deploying clinical software.

components.title: SDLC Change Integrity
components.remarks: Ensures medical software integrity without implying safety.

components.title: SDLC Assurance
components.remarks: Provides assurance evidence that does not substitute for clinical validation.

components.title: SDLC Operations Handover
components.remarks: Transfers custody without enabling clinical use.

roles.title: IoMT SDLC Architecture
roles.remarks: Defines medical SDLC constraints and clinical safety boundaries.

roles.title: IoMT SDLC Governance
roles.remarks: Owns medical software lifecycle and validation requirements.

roles.title: Clinical Authorization Authority
roles.remarks: Provides explicit approval before any clinical software activation.

roles.title: Regulatory Compliance Authority
roles.remarks: Ensures alignment with FDA, EU MDR, and other regulatory obligations.

roles.title: IoMT SDLC Operations
roles.remarks: Manages delivery tooling without activation authority.

roles.title: IoMT Deployment Operations
roles.remarks: Executes controlled clinical deployment under explicit authorization.

control-implementation.remarks: Controls are satisfied through Secure‑SDLC interpretation of NIST SP 800‑53 control families SA, CM, IA, AU, SI, and SR, with patient safety and clinical authorization enforced via Secure‑Resilience and Secure‑Device SSPPs.
